allow.line: | O-E10 | **`L_coil`, the relay coil inductance. An INVENTED CONSTANT — no primary source states a coil inductance, or any inductance, anywhere in the corpus.** The architecture models the coil as a **series R-L branch with coil current as the carried state**, and makes pull-in and drop-out thresholds on quantized *current* rather than on a DC voltage (`architecture.md` §3.3, §4.1). **Why it matters.** It is O-E1's own named fallback made concrete — the mechanism, not a flourish. On `MV601-REF-A`'s own numbers a lamp-fed coil is **2.1× slower** to reach pull-in and sits at 94% of its own asymptote, so the Book IV counter loses carry races that Book I Experiment 9 — where the operator holds the button and there is no race — cannot lose. It is also the one element that makes the two release paths fall out of **a single solve with no rate-selection branch** (`architecture.md` §4.2): an open coil collapses in about one tick, while a coil turned off by short-circuiting it — which is how *every* flip-flop in the corpus turns a relay off — freewheels on `L/R_coil` and releases 2–5× slower, the slugged-relay effect `components.md` §9.3 describes. Delete `L_coil` and both behaviours revert to hand-written rules with no equation behind them. **What was tried.** The nine-document sweep behind G1 and O-E2 found no coil resistance, coil voltage, pull-in or drop-out figure; it likewise found **no inductance, no henry figure, and no relay identification** beyond SDC part 6437 (*Relay, $6.00*), which is a price, not a datasheet. Nothing on paper can produce this number, and none was inferred from one — **it was chosen** | `MV601-REF-A` extended with a new `L_coil_uh` key, tagged `[unverified]`, living in **`data/profiles/*.json` — never a constant in code** (`architecture.md` §10). Indicative 0.9–1.5 H; the shipped profile carries 1.2 H. The value is deliberately **not pinned in prose**: `tools/check-profile.ts` solves for it against ordering constraints R1 and R6, AT-11 and the 2–5× release band, and refuses to load a profile that fails. Reasoning: an R-L companion is **exact at DC**, so adding inductance does not perturb the DC operating point and leaves AT-01 untouched — the constant buys the timing mechanism without paying anything on the thresholds. **The standing risk, stated rather than buried:** the counter's failure could instead be produced by the six per-relay offsets `dV_relay_mv`, with `L_coil` doing no work at all. `architecture.md` §4.3 runs two controls — the spread zeroed, and the spread rotated by one relay index — and if the counter stops failing under either, the spread is the mechanism, this fallback has not earned its keep, and the plan stops rather than tuning around it | An LCR or bridge reading across `E`–`F` on a surviving unit — the direct measurement, and part of the same session that closes O-E2. Failing that: pull-in **time** at lamp-divided versus full-rail drive, which tests the prediction directly (~2× slower, and diverging as rail sag pushes `i_final` toward `i_pullin`); a scope on a real carry cascade; or identification of SDC part 6437 against a 1961 datasheet. **What would overturn it:** a measured inductance small enough that a lamp-fed coil never loses a race — that does not retune the profile, it **re-opens O-E1** with the timing explanation dead; or a real unit whose counter mis-counts **uniformly** rather than at the stages O-T5 predicts, which kills the serial-race model this constant exists to serve |
